item.title: Quantum banking system for secure cash withdrawal
item.description: arXiv:2611.03706v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A quantum-secure withdrawal framework is presented by replacing reproducible classical credentials with quantum tokens for authentication. The protocol integrates token generation, authentication, and verification into the existing banking workflow using experimentally motivated quantum control techniques. This mitigates card cloning, credential theft, and counterfeiting.
item.dc:creator: Vineet Kumar

item.title: Optimised finite key for satellite up-link entangled quantum key distribution
item.description: arXiv:2611.03788v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Entanglement-based quantum key distribution from ground to satellite has been proposed as a scalable primitive for global quantum networks and will be demonstrated as part of the imminent QEYSSat mission. Both theoretical studies and experimental emulations have shown that a significant asymptotic key rate can be expected. In this work we investigate this scenario with a more rigorous security analysis taking into account the finite size effects that arise from short block lengths common in satellite transmission. Our findings suggest a slight alteration of the optimal source operation when informed by finite statistics as opposed to the asymptotic regime, notably that the pump power should be slightly lowered. We quantify the annual key rate based on a dynamically optimised source operation for the Heriot-Watt ground station and several satellite parameters. We find an improved annual key rate when accumulating all raw key material before extracting a secure key instead of doing so for each overpass. We ultimately show that QEYSSat will be able to generate a significant secure annual key with both strategies.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Jaeken, Faris Redza, Stefan B\"auml, Daniel K. L. Oi, Alessandro Fedrizzi, Jasminder S. Sidhu

item.title: Long-range entangled criticality from coherent errors
item.description: arXiv:2611.03811v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We find that coherent error can induce a phase transition from the clean surface code phase into an extended long-range entangled critical regime with diverging Markov length. To demonstrate this, we establish two general results of independent interest. The first relates topology and quantum information to mixed-state entanglement: we show that when a noise channel acting on a topological code preserves a higher-form symmetry and nonzero coherent information, the noisy state for generic logical input is long-range entangled. The second generalizes the local recovery construction based on finite Markov length to any locally parameterized family, thus encompassing local Lindbladian evolution, coherent errors followed by syndrome dephasing, and thermal states. We apply these results to the honeycomb surface code, in which we find an extended long-range entangled critical regime that is a quasi-long-ranged counterpart of 1-form strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking. As a byproduct of these studies, we relate the conditional mutual information to conductance in a Majorana network model.
item.dc:creator: Amir-Reza Negari, Subhayan Sahu, Jan Behrends, Benjamin B\'eri, Timothy H. Hsieh

item.title: Entanglement-Aware Quantum Circuit Optimization through Globally Optimal Partitioning
item.description: arXiv:2611.03845v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a scalable framework for globally optimal quantum-circuit partitioning and entanglement-aware block resynthesis. The partitioning problem is formulated as an integer linear program over qubit-feasible convex subcircuits, supporting objectives such as minimizing the number of partitions or a weighted execution cost. The resulting partition selection is exact over the enumerated feasible candidates and their computed costs when the ILP is solved to proven optimality. The selected partitions are resynthesized using an operator-Schmidt rank (OSR) based synthesis technique, which exploits their internal entanglement structure. We compare the end-to-end integer linear programming (ILP)--OSR workflow with BQSKit while identifying their different routing methods, and separately compare local OSR and BQSKit synthesis on matched three- and four-qubit unitaries. On the frozen sample of 772 local unitary targets, OSR produces 741 verified syntheses versus 617 for BQSKit, and matches or improves the CNOT count in all 617 jointly verified pairs. These results demonstrate that globally optimal partition selection combined with entanglement-aware resynthesis improves circuit quality and extends block-based optimization to problem sizes that are impractical for existing optimization workflows.
item.dc:creator: Gregory Morse, Muhammad Al Farizi, Jakab N\'adori, L\'aszl\'o Hajas, Tam\'as Kozsik, Peter Rakyta

item.title: High-fidelity quantum gate learning via physics-informed neural networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.03851v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a physics-informed neural network (PINN) approach for high-fidelity quantum gate learning in both one- and two-qubit systems. We train a PINN using the time-dependent Schr\"{o}dinger equation, where smooth control fields with fixed boundary conditions are obtained by minimizing a loss function that considers model dynamics, gate error, physical constraints, regularization terms, and multiple initial conditions. Training considers pairs of mutually unbiased bases, while independent validation combines Haar-random input states with the average gate fidelity. Unitary simulations yield an average gate infidelity of $8.49\times10^{-8}$ for Hadamard and values between $3.39\times10^{-7}$ and $4.96\times10^{-6}$ for controlled-NOT under $XX$, $YY$, and $ZZ$ interactions. We examine how the learned control fields depend on the coupling, training configuration, and available local fields, including five exchange-type dipolar scenarios. We test the learned control fields under the Lindblad master equation with dephasing and amplitude damping, theoretically reproducing the expected first-order fidelity loss in the weak-dissipation regime. Finally, boundary-adapted Chebyshev expansions represent 139 learned controls with a minimum common count of $K_\ast=24$ coefficients per control for all eleven family-averaged mean squared errors to fall below $10^{-6}$. Separately, square-pulse and Strang propagation at $K=30$ preserve all 31 continuous polynomial references within infidelity $10^{-5}$ at $N=128$ and all larger tested resolutions, under both sampling rules. These results connect multi-state gate synthesis, control-resource characterization, and compact square-pulse playback.
item.dc:creator: Luis Fabra, Cristian E. Susa, Alcides Montoya, Ariel Norambuena

item.title: Hardware-Aware Design and Layout Selection in Quantum Reservoir Computing for Insurance Claims Forecasting
item.description: arXiv:2611.03891v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) processes temporal information through quantum dynamics, but it remains unclear whether small QRC models can forecast real data competitively with classical models and whether their predictions survive the transfer from ideal simulation to noisy hardware. We address both questions for a six-qubit gate-based reservoir that forecasts next-day motor-insurance claim counts. Five reservoir candidates were selected and frozen using hardware-native interaction graphs, Trotterized Ising dynamics, memory and measurement-robustness criteria, circuit cost, and calibrated-noise screening. On 232 held-out test days, the ideal candidates reached root-mean-square errors (RMSEs) of 5.66-6.12 claims/day, compared with 5.36 for ridge regression. For four of the five, the difference from ridge was not significant under a 95% block bootstrap, and their accuracy was comparable with classical recurrent and reservoir baselines. On the 156-qubit IBM Kingston processor, we ran 63 evaluations in 21 paired rounds, comparing hardware-aware, random-native, and Qiskit optimization level 1 layouts. Hardware-aware placement gave lower RMSE than Qiskit in every round, with a maximum transfer distortion of 7.59 claims/day (11.84 for Qiskit), and avoided the severe transfer failures seen for some random layouts. Most of the hardware distortion appeared as a systematic forecast shift, which a short hardware probe on training inputs detected before the test runs. Longer replay windows raised circuit cost without a consistent gain in forecasting accuracy or hardware transfer. Small QRC models can thus reach competitive accuracy on this task, and hardware-aware layout selection makes their transfer to IBM Kingston more consistent.
item.dc:creator: Ren\'ata Rusn\'akov\'a, Eugen \v{S}lapak, Gaurav K. Pandey, Juraj Gazda

item.title: Unital qubit channels are $3$-noisy
item.description: arXiv:2611.03894v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The algebraic and environmental characteristics of mixed unitary quantum operations are investigated. It is established that the composition of two uniformly n-mixed unitary channels is itself n-noisy, and this n-noisy property is shown to be an invariant under unitary equivalence. Furthermore, by utilizing majorization and the divisibility of Kraus rank-four unital qubit channels, we demonstrate that any unital qubit channel can be physically simulated using a three-dimensional maximally mixed environment. Together, these results advance the classification and physical realization of noisy quantum channels.
item.dc:creator: Indu Bala, Preeti Parashar, Swapan Rana

item.title: Analog quantum simulation of paraparticle statistics
item.description: arXiv:2611.03908v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bosonic and fermionic quantum statistics describe all known elementary and emergent particles in three dimensions, although many attempts have been made to discover other valid quantum statistical frameworks. One recent formulation proposes "$R$-paraparticles," indistinguishable particles with nonlocal internal degrees of freedom governed by generalized exchange rules [Wang and Hazzard, Nature 637, 314 (2025)]. Here, we emulate a species of paraparticle that exhibits a generalized Pauli exclusion principle using a superconducting qubit lattice. We confirm its unique quantum statistics by measuring a $180^\circ$ phase shift under paraparticle exchange, observing antibunching independent of internal degrees of freedom under two-particle interference at a beamsplitter, and finding a thermal occupation inconsistent with both Bose-Einstein and Fermi-Dirac statistics. These results demonstrate that parastatistics are observable on quantum simulation platforms, further motivating their use to explore theorized new phases of matter.
item.dc:creator: Gyunghun Kim, Cora N. Barrett, Sarah E. Muschinske, Junyoung An, Helin Zhang, Ilan T. Rosen, Rabindra Das, Michael A. Gingras, David K. Kim, Bethany M. Niedzielski, Meghan Schuldt, Jonilyn L. Yoder, Mollie E. Schwartz, Kyle Serniak, Jeffrey A. Grover, Max Hays, William D. Oliver

item.title: Non-Hermitian effective dynamics from post-selection protocols
item.description: arXiv:2611.03910v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multiple seemingly distinct frameworks are commonly proposed to explain the emergence of effective non-Hermitian dynamics in quantum systems coupled to an environment. Furthermore, it remains contested how to properly calculate expectation values or whether thermal equilibrium states exist in non-Hermitian systems. In this work, we show that Feshbach projection, the Lindblad master equation, and the ancilla approach can all be understood through the Kraus map formalism, leading to non-Hermitian time evolution if an appropriate post-selection procedure is enforced. After first deriving an exact expression for the conditional system dynamics, we discuss the approximations employed in each approach and the classes of non-Hermitian Hamiltonians that can be obtained. Within this framework, we physically justify the consistency of the right-right formalism (as opposed to the biorthogonal one) for calculating expectation values. Finally, we demonstrate that the traditional notion of thermodynamic equilibrium is not applicable to general non-Hermitian systems. Consequently, stationary states are characterized as non-equilibrium steady states, which should not be conflated with system-projected thermal states of the system-environment composite.
item.dc:creator: Apostolos Siskou, Volker Meden

item.title: Pump quantization changes optimal measurements for quantum sensing
item.description: arXiv:2611.03943v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Standard analyses of quantum phase sensing often neglect the overhead of generating squeezed-light by treating the pump as an undepleted classical resource. Realistically, the pump is a quantum object that undergoes significant depletion and entangles with the produced squeezed light, raising the question of how the crossover from a classical to a quantum pump limits the quantum advantage in sensing. Contrary to prior analyses, we show that quantum advantage persists despite pump quantization, but depends critically on the nonlinear $(\chi^{(2)})$ source dynamics. In particular, we demonstrate that Heisenberg scaling emerges in the regime of strong pump depletion, rather than maximum signal squeezing. At maximum squeezing, the quantum Fisher information (QFI) for interferometric sensing of an unknown phase scales as $N^{3/2}$, where $N$ is the pump photon number, surpassing the shot-noise limit but establishing that squeezing itself is insufficient to attain Heisenberg scaling of $N^2$. At maximal pump depletion, where the signal flux is maximized, the QFI scales as $N^2$. In this regime, standard photon counting is suboptimal, while a joint nonlinear measurement of the entire pump-signal system is shown to achieve Heisenberg scaling. Our work shows that pump quantization changes both the optimal operating point and the measurement strategies required to preserve a realistic quantum advantage in phase estimation and, more broadly, many-body quantum dynamics.
item.dc:creator: S. A. Wadood, L. Bello, T. Ilias, J. W. Fleischer

item.title: The Impact of Internal Electric Fields on Accurate Diamond Magnetometry
item.description: arXiv:2611.03984v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center spin ensembles are a promising platform for accurate vector magnetometry, as they offer measurements referenced to a spin Hamiltonian in an anisotropic crystal with native vector sensing capabilities. However, charged dopants within the diamond produce random internal electric fields (RIEFs) that shift NV spin-transition frequencies, and their impact on the accuracy of NV magnetometry has not been investigated. Here, we characterize RIEFs' effect on NV spin-transition spectra and propose an analytical fitting function to improve accuracy in their presence. We build a Monte Carlo RIEF model that reproduces the asymmetric lineshapes observed in experimental optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) spectra, and use it as a testbed to quantify RIEF-induced errors by simulating ODMR spectra including RIEFs and comparing reconstructed magnetic fields to the known model input. With standard analysis approaches, we observe systematic errors exceeding the g-factor uncertainty in fields below $\sim$ 5 mT, while the proposed fitting function reduces the error by nearly an order of magnitude. Our results demonstrate that RIEFs can play a significant role in the systematic error budget for NV magnetometry, and offer a path towards improved accuracy in NV quantum sensing.
item.dc:creator: Jack Faller, Daphne Freda Gavras, Andrew Lowther, Romain Ruhlmann, Lilian Childress

item.title: Adaptive Qubit Encoding for Continuous-Variable Quantum Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2611.03987v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optimizing continuous-variable functions on qubit-based quantum hardware requires a finite representation of the search space and a solver-compatible representation of the objective function. Fixed-grid discretizations provide a direct encoding, but restrict the search to a predefined range and resolution; at the same time, constructing a compact Hamiltonian for a general continuous-variable objective can be impractical. Here, we introduce a framework for continuous-variable optimization tailored to qubit-based quantum architectures. The method combines an adaptive discretization with an iterative local mapping of the objective function onto an effective spin-glass Hamiltonian. We assess the approach on unconstrained and constrained instances of the $n$-dimensional Gramacy-Lee benchmark, and on a proof-of-concept inverse-planning problem in intensity-modulated radiotherapy (IMRT) for cancer treatment. The results show that this framework can produce competitive solutions, supporting its use as a flexible mapping strategy for continuous-variable optimization in qubit-based quantum and quantum-inspired pipelines.
item.dc:creator: Samuele Cavinato, Marco Tesoro, Gianluca Morettini, Marta Paiusco, Alessandro Scaggion, Simone Montangero, Ilaria Siloi

item.title: Tight Quasiprobabilistic Entropic Uncertainty Relations for Discrete Quantum Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.04009v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It was conjectured by Wehrl and proven by Lieb that the Shannon differential entropy of the Husimi function of a continuous-variable quantum state is lower bounded by the value it takes on coherent states. This corroborates the intuition, familiar from Heisenberg's uncertainty relations, that coherent states are minimal uncertainty states. The analogous statement for the Wigner function would be that the Wigner differential entropy of states with a positive Wigner function is bounded below by the entropy of pure Gaussian states. This was conjectured a decade ago, but recently disproven. Here, we prove the analogous statement for Kirkwood-Dirac distributions with mutually unbiased bases and for the Gross-Wigner distributions. For these discrete systems, the entropy-minimizing role is played by the pure states with positive quasiprobability distributions. Further, we prove that Kirkwood-Dirac distributions with large nonpositivity have large uncertainty.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan J. Thio, Stephan De Bi\`evre, Crispin H. W. Barnes, David R. M. Arvidsson-Shukur

item.title: Gaussian Quantum Integrated Sensing and Communication
item.description: arXiv:2611.04047v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a quantum integrated sensing and communication problem over an optical link in which a low-power transmitter simultaneously communicates with a receiver and identifies the range of a defect producing a backscattered signal. We model the system as a lossy thermal-noise bosonic channel, in which the target, modeled as a beamsplitter, affects the timing of the backscattered signal through its location. Motivated by the envisioned deployment of entanglement-enabled quantum networks, we develop two protocols that allow the transmitter to leverage shared Gaussian entanglement, in the form of independent two-mode squeezed vacuum states or coupled three-mode squeezed vacuum states, to assist both sensing and communication. Since entanglement is known to enhance sensing, as demonstrated in quantum illumination, and to increase communication rates through entanglement-assisted communication, the transmitter faces a trade-off in allocating its entanglement resources between the two tasks. Our main results characterize these trade-offs under the proposed protocols in terms of achievable communication rate/sensing error-exponent regions, which outperform time-sharing schemes and demonstrate a quantum advantage.
item.dc:creator: Tuna Erdo\u{g}an, Shi-Yuan Wang, Shang-Jen Su, Matthieu R. Bloch

item.title: Runtime Compilation for Quantum Circuits with PQF-Enabled $R_z$ Synthesis
item.description: arXiv:2611.04075v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing (FTQC) using surface codes, reducing $T$-count is critical for efficient computation due to the high cost of $T$-state distillation. Probabilistic Quantum Circuit with Fallback (PQF) synthesis significantly lowers $T$-counts compared to standard protocols like Gridsynth, but introduces high circuit dynamism through extra gates inserted at runtime. This dynamism invalidates static compile-time routing, as these new $T$ gates require dynamic lattice surgery routing to establish non-intersecting ancilla paths to $T$-state factories while minimizing total execution time. To address this, we introduce $\text{R}^2$-PQF, a Runtime Routing protocol for PQF-synthesized quantum circuits. $\text{R}^2$-PQF dynamically routes gates layer-by-layer, computing paths during the execution of the previous logical timestep. To satisfy the strict computational window of $\sim t_{lattice\_surgery} + t_{reaction}$ and non-intersectionality constraints, we implement a Wavefront Breadth-First Search (W-BFS) and synthesise it on a 500MHz FPGA and 2 GHz ASIC. For a clock cycle of 2GHz, we achieve a median logical time-step of $1.51 \mu s$ for a 300 qubit Ising Hamiltonian circuit, demonstrating that $\text{R}^2$-PQF successfully resolves the vast majority of paths (with rare exceptions) within the execution window and enables the $T$-count benefits of PQF without latency penalties. Compared to a baseline stalling-based solution (the only no-runtime-recomputation solution), $\text{R}^2$-PQF speeds up circuit execution by $1.34\times$ on average and up to $1.76 \times$.
item.dc:creator: Siddharth Dangwal, Christopher Kang, Jad Habhab, Ritvik Sharma, Frederic T. Chong, Gokul Subramanian Ravi

item.title: Anti-distinguishability of quantum channels
item.description: arXiv:2611.04105v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study single-query perfect anti-distinguishability/exclusion tasks of finite quantum channel ensembles, primarily using associated Choi operators and process POVMs. Weak perfect anti-distinguishability requires each measurement outcome to exclude an ensemble candidate with certainty, whereas the strong form additionally requires every candidate to have an exclusion outcome occurring with non-zero probability. For pairs of channels, both coincide with perfect distinguishability, whereas larger ensembles exhibit separations. We derive Choi-operator-support-based obstructions: weak exclusion requires at least two rank-deficient Choi operators, while strong exclusion requires the support of every candidate Choi operator to be strictly contained in the joint Choi support. The common Choi support must also lie in the kernel of the PPOVM normalisation. For commuting Choi operators, this condition is sufficient for weak exclusion when the normalisation also commutes with them. Conversely, a nonzero admixture of the same noise channel into every candidate precludes weak exclusion for any probe. We apply these results to measure-and-prepare, state-space contraction, Pauli, and replacer channels. In particular, the full permutation-channel ensemble of an unlabeled POVM is strongly anti-distinguishable exactly when some POVM effect is rank-deficient, while replacer-channel exclusion reduces to state exclusion. A Choi-commuting ensemble exhibits strong exclusion with an unassisted probe although no positive-definite PPOVM normalisation permits even weak exclusion. In contrast, commuting qubit phase gates, whose Choi operators need not commute, admit exact convex-hull criteria for weak and strong exclusion, both attainable without assistance.
item.dc:creator: Ardra Ajitha Vijayan, Nidhin Sudarsanan Ragini

item.title: Entanglement Allocation for Quantum Integrated Sensing and Communication
item.description: arXiv:2611.04128v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Jointly supporting communication and distributed sensing over a shared, limited pool of entanglement resources is an attractive prospect for future quantum networks. We develop a network-level quantum integrated sensing and communication (Q-ISAC) framework in which a quantum base station dynamically allocates elementary Bell pairs between communication users and distributed sensing. Sensing resources are adaptively partitioned among multiple GHZ probes with dynamically selected sizes and sensing-node assignments. We derive an effective quantum Fisher information model accounting for probabilistic fusion, transmission loss, and memory decoherence, and formulate a finite-horizon allocation problem subject to communication QoS, expected sensing-information, sensing-reliability, and hardware constraints. A hierarchical constrained proximal policy optimization (HC-PPO) framework combines learned discrete sensing allocation with analytical continuous communication allocation. Numerical results show that GHZ probing requires approximately $27$--30% fewer sensing qubits than separable probing under modest probe-size caps and 65-67% fewer at the highest considered target under the same sensing requirements. Adaptive multi-GHZ partitioning provides greater robustness than single-GHZ sensing, while adaptive communication--sensing sharing outperforms the evaluated fixed splits. The proposed HC-PPO framework satisfies the joint requirements in at least 99.9% of test instances across the considered sensing targets and fusion probabilities. Monte Carlo evaluation separately shows that realized terminal information reached its target in 96-98% of realizations, distinguishing expected-information satisfaction from realized sensing performance.
item.dc:creator: Shiva Kazemi Taskooh, Mehdi Monemi, Ekram Hossain, Georges Kaddoum, Mehdi Rasti

item.title: Quantum identity authentication protocol via perturbed probability amplitudes
item.description: arXiv:2611.04129v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum identity authentication is an effective solution for establishing mutual trust between communicating parties in the post-quantum era. To address the risk of partial secret information leakage under special measurements, this paper designs a quantum identity authentication protocol based on perturbed probability amplitudes. The protocol first proposes a method of encoding a random sequence onto the probability amplitudes of quantum entangled states, forming perturbed probability amplitudes, thereby reducing the involvement of shared information between the sender and receiver. Furthermore, it presents a method for generating n-bit random authentication information based on the n-bit pre-shared information, enhancing the randomness of the authentication information relative to an attacker. The proposed protocol can resist impersonation attack, CNOT attack, and entanglement measurement attack, and ensures backward security. Under equivalent security conditions, the amount of shared information is 1/n that in Chen et al.'s scheme and half that in Dutta et al.'s scheme. And each bit of the secret message has no risk of leakage under special measurements. It can also be extended to a bi-directional quantum identity authentication protocol.
item.dc:creator: Xiangqun Fu, Zheng Han, Hongwei Li, Chun Zhou, Shuo Zhang, Jianhong Shi, Tan Li, Wansu Bao

item.title: Initialization-controlled fault sensitivity and force-balance plateaus in noisy variational quantum optimization
item.description: arXiv:2611.04198v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study deep variational circuits for a periodic Heisenberg chain under local gate depolarization, at depths where noiseless training is coherently exact. Full-width initializations reach low coherent error faster than circuits with confined transverse generators, but incur a larger noise shift and need an order of magnitude more updates for noisy convergence. In many-body-localization-inspired initialization, bounding the initial transverse generator amplitudes keeps the operator support localized and suffices for low-fragility optimization, so longitudinal disorder and Floquet layer repetition are unnecessary. The fault-erasure fraction, the mean fraction of coherent energy removed per fault, sets the effective visibility through a parameter-free exponential model. Full-width circuits start with delocalized operator support, and once coherent energy builds up, each fault erases nearly all of it. Initially, their noise-induced gradient almost uniformly attenuates the coherent gradient, so coherent descent proceeds at the noiseless rate. They then stall on a high-noise force-balance plateau, where finite coherent and noise-induced gradients cancel to first order. At late times all initializations reach the same fault-erasure fraction and noisy-error band, but operator support contracts more slowly, at a rate set by the plateau residence time.
item.dc:creator: Longhui Shen, Fangzhou Jin, Bin Guo

item.title: Information-Geometric Representation of Upper Bounds on Fluctuation Growth in Open Quantum Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.04263v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Building on our earlier results for closed quantum systems, we investigate the dynamical evolution of quantum fluctuations and their connections to Fisher information and the quantum operations describing open-system dynamics. Starting from a general expression for the time derivative of an observable's uncertainty, we derive an alternative upper bound on fluctuation growth in an open quantum system using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality. The resulting bound separates contributions from the evolution of the quantum state and the explicit time dependence of the observable, reducing to a known result for closed-system dynamics. We then establish a connection between fluctuation dynamics and quantum Fisher information by decomposing the density operator and the symmetric logarithmic derivative (SLD) into coherent and incoherent contributions, which leads to a bound relating the evolution of observable uncertainty to the coherent and incoherent components of the Fisher information, providing an information-geometric interpretation of fluctuation growth. To connect fluctuation dynamics with quantum operations governing open-system evolutions, we derive the time evolution of the eigenvalues of the density operator in terms of Kraus operators. Using the infinitesimal-time relation between Kraus and Lindblad operators, we obtain a corresponding expression for the eigenvalue dynamics in terms of Lindblad operators. This formulation directly relates changes in the density operator eigenvalues to the quantum processes acting on the system. We then study the results using some examples. Our results provide a framework connecting observable fluctuation growth, Fisher information, and the Kraus and Lindblad descriptions of quantum evolution, offering a route toward understanding how specific quantum channels influence the information and fluctuations available in an evolving quantum system.
item.dc:creator: Newshaw Bahreyni, Paul M. Alsing

item.title: Reasoning about Shared-Qubit Concurrency in Quantum Computing
item.description: arXiv:2611.04274v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we develop a semantic model for the parallel execution of quantum circuits, providing a formal foundation for studying shared-qubit concurrency in quantum computing. As in classical shared-memory concurrency, parallel quantum circuits may interfere with one another through operations on shared qubits. However, quantum entanglement and the noncommutativity of quantum operations introduce additional challenges for reasoning about their correctness. To address these challenges, we generalise the classical Owicki-Gries method to quantum computing at the level of quantum circuits. Our approach enables compositional reasoning about parallel quantum circuits by separating the verification of individual components from the analysis of interference between them. We formulate proof rules for establishing the correctness of parallel quantum circuits and prove their soundness with respect to the proposed semantic model.
item.dc:creator: Mingsheng Ying

item.title: An example of universal braiding in Links--Gould topological quantum computation
item.description: arXiv:2611.04290v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a universal quantum computational encoding via braiding in Links--Gould fusion spaces associated to $U_q^H(\mathfrak{sl}(2|1))$ where $q$ is on the unit circle and is not a root of unity. The construction uses only neglectons and is realized in the morphism spaces $\mathrm{Hom}_{U_q^H}(V(0,\alpha),V(0,-\frac{1}{2})^{\otimes 2N}\otimes V(0,\alpha)).$ Under explicit positivity and arithmetic constraints these spaces admit a $2^N$-dimensional computational subspace with a positive definite Hermitian form. We prove single-qubit density in $\mathrm{U}(2,1)$ and approximate arbitrary unitary operators on $N$-qubit computational subspaces with arbitrarily small leakage. The calculations use explicit inclusions, projections, and Hermitian pairings without requiring $F$-matrices.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Harper, Ben-Michael Kohli

item.title: Approximate Synthetic Spectra of Quantum Systems Associated with Compact Lie Groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.04306v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: How can noncommuting quantum observables retain the geometry of a classical phase space? Motivated by Mumford's question on approximately macroscopically unique (AMU) states and the work of Lin and Wang, we study synthetic spectra of position--momentum and angular-momentum systems. Under the hypotheses of their AMU theorems, nonempty synthetic spectra yield AMU states. For sufficiently small $\hbar$, the position--momentum spectrum fills the plane, while the angular-momentum spectrum contains any prescribed ball. The latter calculation leads to compact Lie groups: we prove that highest-weight coadjoint orbits lie in regional synthetic spectra under an explicit variance bound. Function-space representations of $SU(n)$, $SO(n)$, and $Sp(n)$ provide further examples.
item.dc:creator: Junyang Liu, Hang Wang, Houjin Wang, Haoran Xu

item.title: A Conditional Quantum Kac-Bernstein Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2611.04363v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a conditional quantum Kac-Bernstein theorem for mixing of two independent, finite-mode bosonic inputs with quantum memories. We characterize exactly when the outputs are conditionally independent given both memories. Each input then decomposes into orthogonal memory sectors sharing a common Gaussian state on the physical system and a bosonic memory factor, up to sector-dependent physical displacements. In particular, triviality of the common bosonic factor implies separability of the inputs, as occurs whenever either memory has finite-dimensional support.
item.dc:creator: Hesam Hosseini, Jinpei Zhao, Masahito Hayashi

item.title: On the Hardness of Approximate Quantum Circuit Membership and Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2611.04381v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum circuit optimization is an indispensable component of the quantum software stack, used to reduce noise, maximize performance, alleviate costs of quantum error correction, or target specific hardware. A related problem is approximate membership: for a fixed set of unitaries $S$, decide whether a given circuit $C$ is within distance $\varepsilon$ of a unitary in $S$ under some metric $m$. Membership is a special case of optimization, where $S$ is a set of unitaries implementable at no cost (e.g., with noise-minimal circuits, or without magic states). Janzing, Wocjan, and Beth (Int. J. Quantum Inf., 2005) showed that, for the operator metric, the case $S=\{I\}$ (approximate identity) is QMA-complete when $C$ is promised to be either close to the identity or far from it. We generalize this setting in three directions: (i) promise-free inputs, (ii) besides $S=\{I\}$, sets $S$ containing only Clifford unitaries, or only generalized permutation matrices (i.e., no superposition), and (iii) the trace-based, spectral, and operator metrics. We show that, in all cases, approximate membership is PP-hard for wide ranges of $\varepsilon$, provided $C$'s gate-set can implement Clifford+T, as the gate-sets of standard hardware do. If $S=\{I\}$, or if $S$ contains only generalized permutation matrices, $I\in S$, and $m$ is a trace-based distance, PP-hardness holds for all non-trivial $\varepsilon$. If $S=\{I\}$ and $m$ is a trace-based distance, PP-hardness holds even for circuits over classical-reversible gate-sets. Our results indicate that approximate membership is harder over promise-free inputs than the QMA-complete promise version, and that this hardness persists across quantum resources (any gates, non-Clifford, superposition) and distance metrics. They directly imply PP-hardness of circuit optimization when minimizing total, non-Clifford, or superposition gate depth or count.
item.dc:creator: Adam Husted Kjelstr{\o}m, Jaco van de Pol, Andreas Pavlogiannis

item.title: Reducing the arithmetic cost of quantum derivative pricing with language-model circuit design
item.description: arXiv:2611.04431v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum amplitude estimation can estimate expected discounted payoffs with quadratically fewer oracle calls than Monte Carlo, but each call requires coherent computation. We use language-model-assisted circuit design to reduce reversible payoff arithmetic for a three-asset worst-of autocallable and a target accrual redemption forward (TARF). The constructions retain compact integer representations of market paths alongside contract history, reconstructing quantities temporarily for contract decisions and payoff-angle evaluation. Relative to matched internal references, the factor-sum autocallable and windowed TARF circuits reduce the product of Toffoli count and peak logical qubits $(N_{Tof} Q_{max})$ by factors of 2.39 and 4.84, respectively. At a second autocallable setting, fresh search recovers a 1.35-fold saving after the tested fixed adaptation loses its advantage. For the factor-sum circuit, we prove exact coherent execution of its integer specification for every input, incoming accumulator and measurement record, with clean workspace and phase cancellation. A separate lattice calculation gives a numerical angle-tolerance-violation probability of 6.248e-8 and evaluates pricing bias under the declared loading law, with bounded omission but no certified numerical enclosure. The results connect compact representations to lower-cost payoff arithmetic and separately assessed logical and financial correctness. Their resource scope excludes loading, payoff rotation and estimation.
item.dc:creator: Monit Sharma, Hoong Chun Lau

item.title: Universal Free-Electron-Sideband Control
item.description: arXiv:2611.04432v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Advances in free-electron quantum optics are establishing free electrons as a versatile quantum resource. Photon-induced near-field electron microscopy (PINEM) interactions and free drift provide elementary operations for shaping the longitudinal electron wavefunction, yet their full control capabilities remain unexplored. Here, we prove that a finite sequence of alternating monochromatic PINEM interactions and free drifts can approximate any prescribed inner-product-preserving map from a finite-dimensional input subspace into the full ideal electron-sideband Hilbert space to arbitrary accuracy. We therefore call the protocol PINEMAD (PINEM And Drift). This framework encompasses state preparation, unitary gates, and isometric encoding. We further show numerically that parameter optimization enables high-fidelity state preparation at finite electron energy spreads, using experimentally accessible coupling strengths and tabletop-scale total drift lengths. These results establish electron energy sidebands as a programmable quantum resource.
item.dc:creator: Tong Shen, Zhexin Zhao, Meng Xiao

item.title: Hybrid Quantum--Classical Pauli-Correlator Architecture for Image Reconstruction
item.description: arXiv:2611.04442v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the Pauli-Correlator Autoencoder (PCAE), a hybrid quantum--classical architecture for image reconstruction. PCAE splits an image into patches and compresses each patch as a matrix product state (MPS). A small quantum circuit turns each compressed patch into a few measured numbers, and a classical neural network rebuilds the patch from these numbers and the patch position. A learnable energy term, taken from physics, is added to training and tracked as training proceeds. Two versions place the six qubits on a line (PCAE1D) or on a grid (PCAE2D). An averaging step makes the PCAE2D features follow rotations and reflections of the image exactly. Trained on one image at a time, PCAE2D rebuilds images from six public datasets with a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 25.8 to 41.6 decibels. On CIFAR-10 images not used in training, a formula-based stand-in for the PCAE2D features performs within 1 decibel of several simpler classical methods. Five trained models also run on real IBM quantum computers without retraining, and rebuild images at 25.90 to 31.52 decibels. A short argument and a synthetic test show that, with a linear final layer, measuring qubits in pairs is needed for targets built from products of inputs. These results show that PCAE works as a hybrid model that rebuilds varied images and runs on today's quantum hardware at the six-qubit scale.
item.dc:creator: Sparsho Chakraborty, Siddhartha Patra

item.title: Broken-Symmetry Reference States for Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization with Near-DMRG Accuracy
item.description: arXiv:2611.04496v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD) accuracy remains limited for strongly correlated systems like iron-sulfur clusters. This accuracy heavily depends on the mean-field reference state, which determines the sampling ansatz and configuration-recovery target. We extend the qcsc-prefect workflow to support a broken-symmetry unrestricted Hartree-Fock (BS-UHF) starting point, derived from atom-localized antiferromagnetic initial guesses. For the $[Fe_4S_4(SCH_3)_4]^{2-}$ cubane (54 electrons, 36 orbitals, 72 data qubits; 88 total qubits), this lowers the mean-field reference by $\approx 534$ mHa relative to the Restricted Hartree-Fock (RHF) solution (-327.0809 vs. -326.5474 Ha). Combined with deep multi-step configuration recovery on ROQUO GPU nodes at subspace dimension $d = 3 \times 10^{10}$, we reach $E = -327.235076$ Ha. This is 4.3 mHa above the finite-$D = 4000$ DMRG value (-327.2393952 Ha) and $\sim 512-517$ mHa below a previous same-active-space RHF-reference SQD calculation. Extrapolating to the $d \to \infty$ limit via a Gaussian-in-log $d$ fitting ansatz gives an asymptotic estimate $E_\infty = -327.244468$ Ha $\pm 1.05$ mHa, just 0.33 mHa above our discarded-weight-extrapolated DMRG estimate ($E_{D\to\infty} = -327.244797$ Ha $\pm 0.46$ mHa), well within their combined $1\sigma$ uncertainty. We characterize the determinant-subspace composition driving convergence, show matching validation on $[Fe_2S_2(SCH_3)_4]^{2-}$, and report multi-HPC execution on Fugaku, Miyabi-G, and ROQUO. We conclude that reference-state preparation, rather than subspace size alone, is a key driver of SQD energy accuracy under strong electronic correlation.
item.dc:creator: Kunal Kumar, Tomonori Shirakawa, Boseong Kim, Ryo Wakizaka, Ikko Hamamura, Mitsuhisa Sato, Seiji Yunoki, Mario Motta, Hiroshi Horii, Yuri Kobayashi

item.title: Motional Decoherence of the internal state of an atom by vacuum and thermal fluctuations of a quantum field: Necessity of a fully relativistic treatment
item.description: arXiv:2611.04512v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a massive object, such as a neutral atom or an Unruh-DeWitt detector, moving at constant speed in a quantum field and investigate how motion affects the quantum coherence of its internal degrees of freedom, manifesting as quantum dispersion in the absence of a quantum field, and decoherence in its presence. Our investigation aims to serve two purposes: One is to obtain the correct results for these effects, which are essential for the design of quantum information processing schemes where the quantum coherence of an atom's internal degrees of freedom is of major concern. The other is to expose the fallacies in commonplace approaches, which start with a non-relativistic calculation and then add on relativistic ``corrections". We first show a fully relativistic calculation of the internal dynamics based on covariance principles, and then one which ignores these principles, often justified by the atom's slow motion. By a direct comparison of results from these two approaches, we identify {significant discrepancies} in a non-relativistic treatment, even at low atomic speeds. The proper procedure, and a much safer one in terms of accuracy, is recommended here: first derive the dynamics and the necessary regularizations within a fully covariant relativistic framework. Only after the exact, internally consistent equations of motion are established should low-velocity limits be extracted from them. Only in this way can all the relativistic effects which matter: time dilation, aberration, non-inertial mass shifts, be systematically preserved, and accurate results obtained.
item.dc:creator: Jen-Tsung Hsiang, Bei-Lok Hu

item.title: Long-lived quantum memories with rare-earth ions doped in crystals
item.description: arXiv:2611.04526v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum memory is a core enabling device for large-scale quantum networks, serving as the fundamental building block for quantum repeaters and transportable quantum memories. Among various physical platforms, rare-earth-ion-doped crystals stand out as one of the most promising solid-state candidates for long-lived photonic quantum memories, owing to their exceptionally long spin coherence time and their compatibility with integration. In this review, we first introduce the physical mechanisms underlying long-lived spin coherence in rare-earth systems, with particular emphasis on the zero-first-order-Zeeman transition and dynamical decoupling techniques. We then review the experimental progress in this field, highlighting three distinct lifetimes--the spin coherence time, the light storage time, and the quantum storage time--and covering experiments that have achieved hour-scale spin coherence, minute- to hour-scale light storage, and minute-scale single-photon-level quantum storage. Finally, we discuss the remaining challenges that hinder the realization of practical long-lived quantum memories, explore potential strategies to overcome these obstacles, and outline the prospects for their future applications in quantum networks.
item.dc:creator: Yu-Yu Sa, Pei-Xi Liu, Zong-Quan Zhou, Chuan-Feng Li

item.title: Decoy-state quantum key distribution with a leaky Mach-Zehnder receiver
item.description: arXiv:2611.04539v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the security of phase-encoded decoy-state BB84 quantum key distribution for a Mach-Zehnder receiver with imbalanced beam splitters and two threshold detectors that leak fine-grained information about the detection patterns. For this, we derive a lower bound on Bob's single-photon contributions and combine it with the decoy-state method and a recent phase-error framework for leaky receivers. The leakage-induced correction to the phase-error rate is independent of channel loss, providing a loss-tolerant treatment of receiver leakage even in the presence of beam-splitter imbalance. Our results provide a practical route toward loss-tolerant security proofs for imperfect QKD receivers in the presence of receiver leakage.
item.dc:creator: Ryohei Mizusawa, \'Alvaro Navarrete, Akihiro Mizutani, Kiyoshi Tamaki

item.title: Wigner-Function Fingerprints of Collective Excitations in Mirror-Terminated Waveguide QED
item.description: arXiv:2611.04553v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the emission profiles of singly excited collective states and propose a matched-mode witnessing protocol in a mirror-terminated waveguide quantum electrodynamics system. The amplitudes and relative phases of the initial collective excitation are encoded in the temporal mode of the emitted single-photon wavepacket, providing a route to state verification through the common waveguide output. We identify the emission mode associated with a chosen target state and employ an auxiliary virtual-cavity representation to evaluate the quantum state of this selected output mode. For a matched initial state, the selected mode contains the emitted single photon, whose Wigner function exhibits a pronounced non-classical negative dip, serving as a distinct fingerprint of the target many-body state. With the reference mode held fixed, different initial configurations yield different photon occupations and phase-space distributions, demonstrating the state selectivity of the protocol. These results connect collective-state verification with temporal-mode analysis of the emitted radiation, offering access to collective coherence with reduced reliance on qubit-resolved correlation measurements.
item.dc:creator: Kuan-Ting Lin, Chen-Yu Lee, Yu-Chen Lin, Ting Hsu, Guin-Dar Lin

item.title: Time-invariant negativity and persistent bound entanglement in a cyclic two-qutrit family
item.description: arXiv:2611.04568v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the entanglement dynamics of two qutrits under collective dephasing for a family of states obtained by mixing a maximally entangled state that lives in the decoherence-free subspace with three nonstationary two-term states sharing a common amplitude ratio $r$. We obtain exact PPT and separability regions along the whole trajectory, a specialization of known results on cyclic sign invariant states, and we supply explicit certificates: a finite product decomposition, three fixed positive-map witnesses, and a closed realignment formula that detects every PPT-entangled state, so that no state is left undecided. The negativity is computed in closed form. It shows that the entanglement is time-invariant, positive and constant from the initial time although the state changes, exactly when the weight of the maximally entangled state exceeds the threshold $U_r=r/(1+r+r^2)$. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of time-invariant entanglement for qutrit--qutrit systems under collective dephasing. For smaller weights the entanglement decays and vanishes at a finite time: the state either becomes separable (entanglement sudden death) or, for $r\neq1$ in an intermediate range, loses distillability suddenly and remains bound entangled at all later times. Every state with negative partial transpose is one-copy distillable by a fixed local projection. The same trajectories arise from the global dephasing map and from a correlated local random-unitary semigroup, although the two channels differ on product inputs. Exact rational benchmarks and embeddings of the Horodecki and Ha--Kye--Park families are provided.
item.dc:creator: Wenlin Zhang, Mazhar Ali, Haobo Ma

item.title: On Random Purifications of Isometries and Channels
item.description: arXiv:2611.04573v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Acorn tricks turn weak quantum resources into stronger "randomized" ones. A recent example is the random purification channel, which turns $t$ copies of a mixed state into $t$ copies of a random purification. We ask whether analogous techniques can turn queries to an isometry into queries to a random unitary completion, or queries to a quantum channel into queries to a random isometry dilation. For an isometry from dimension $N$ to dimension $M$, we give an efficient, stateful simulator for $T$ sequential, forward queries to a fixed Haar random unitary completion. It uses at most one forward isometry query per simulated call, with total trace-distance error $O(T\sqrt{N/(M-T)})$. This lifts isometry query lower bounds to arbitrary unitary completions, and copy complexity lower bounds to forward access to state preparation unitaries, with dimension-dependent loss that can be made arbitrarily small for most applications. Conversely, we construct two distributions on quantum channels distinguishable exactly with two queries to an arbitrary dilation, but requiring exponentially many channel queries for nonnegligible advantage. This rules out efficient simulation of random channel dilations. Our technique also shows that approximating the quantum switch to any constant error below $1/2$ requires exponentially many channel queries, even for identical channels, giving an exponential query advantage for indefinite causal order and improving on Bavaresco et al. (2025). Finally, we show how to "decontrol" controlled forward access to an isometry: any algorithm making controlled queries to $\phi V$ for a random phase $\phi$ can be transformed into one using the same number of uncontrolled forward queries to $V$, generalizing the analogous result for unitaries.
item.dc:creator: Eli Goldin

item.title: Spectral Quantum Memory for Implicit Neural Representations
item.description: arXiv:2611.04574v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Implicit neural representations (INRs) model signals as continuous functions from coordinates to values, but their performance depends strongly on how spectral capacity is allocated. Yet most Quantum INR (QINR) architectures treat spectral components as independent outputs of separate quantum blocks. We introduce the Spectral Quantum Memory Model (SQMM), a memory coupled quantum INR in which sequential hybrid data reuploading layers (bands) communicate through a shared coherent quantum memory register. Each band reads the memory, computes on its own coordinate upload, and writes part of its state back, so later bands can build on the computation of earlier ones. When memory read and write layers are input independent, we prove that the memory state forms an operator valued Fourier series whose support is contained in the Minkowski sum of the initial memory spectrum and the local band spectra. Downstream bands then condition their Fourier coefficients on the spectral content stored by earlier bands, and the memory coupling creates no new primitive frequencies. This theory motivates a spectral memory alignment loss that encourages memory to encode the spectrum expressed by the deployed prefix of the model. Across audio and image reconstruction benchmarks, SQMM improves over compact QINR and INR baselines.
item.dc:creator: Daniel A. Moroz-Broitman, Eliya Nachmani

item.title: Adaptive Self-Optimization of Polarization Efficiency for Low-Power NV Center Thermometers Based on PAS-Q
item.description: arXiv:2611.04588v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond have attracted considerable attention for micro- and nanoscale thermometry owing to their high precision and spatial resolution. However, achieving sufficient electron spin polarization and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) typically requires high-power or long-duration laser excitation, which introduces heating and degrades measurement accuracy and stability. To address this trade-off, a reinforcement learning (RL)-based approach is proposed to optimize spin polarization under low-heating constraints. First, a physical model integrating five-level optical pumping rates and NV spin polarization dynamics is established. A temperature-rise constraint model is then developed based on pulsed optically detected magnetic resonance (P-ODMR) measurements under varying laser powers and pulse widths in an external magnetic field. Subsequently, a Progressive Action-Space Q-learning (PAS-Q) algorithm is employed to explore the parameter space and identify optimal laser power and pulse-width combinations. The agent is trained through numerical simulations and the resulting strategy is implemented in a hardware system. Experimental results demonstrate a 44% reduction in laser-induced heating, a 33% increase in spin polarization rate based on T1 relaxation analysis, and a 71% reduction in optimization time compared with traditional methods. This approach enables efficient spin polarization with reduced laser heating and improved optimization efficiency, and may be extended to other heat-sensitive quantum spin sensors, including silicon-vacancy centers in diamond and divacancy defects in silicon carbide.
item.dc:creator: Yifan Wang, Li Xing, Ruigang Wang, Zheng Qian

item.title: Cooperative Suppression of Two-Particle Excitation by Kerr Nonlinearity and Cavity Loss ion a Driven Holstein-Tavis-Cumming System
item.description: arXiv:2611.04628v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We apply the numerically accurate multiple Davydov Ansatz (multi-$\rm D_2$) method to investigate the nonequilibrium dynamics of an open molecular cavity system using an extended driven-dissipative Holstein-Tavis-Cummings model incorporating Kerr nonlinearity. Our results reveal that the synergy between Kerr nonlinearity and exciton-phonon coupling induces an anharmonic level structure, imposing a stringent energy penalty that isolates the one-excitation manifold. This establishes a robust single-excitation-dominated regime that dynamically manifests photon blockade, characterized by suppression of the pure two-photon state and isolation of the one-excitation manifold. While strong coherent driving induces power broadening that overcomes the nonlinear barrier and opens multiphoton channels, cavity dissipation counteracts this process by acting as a highly selective manifold filter. By preferentially depleting fragile multi-photon states while sheltering single excitations within dissipation-free dark states, the cavity mode decay rate actively cooperates with Kerr nonlinearity to restore and reinforce the photon blockade effect. These findings elucidate the intricate interplay among nonlinearity, driving, and dissipation, offering a theoretical blueprint for engineering robust single-photon sources in open molecular cavity platforms.
item.dc:creator: Zhiyao Qu, Kewei Sun, Youhao Chang, Vladimir Al. Osipov, Yang Zhao, Maxim F. Gelin

item.title: Breakdown of Linearized Dispersion in Waveguide QED
item.description: arXiv:2611.04656v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Exploring interactions between quantum emitters and guided photons, waveguide quantum electrodynamics (wQED) offers a versatile platform for quantum simulation and quantum interconnect. To simplify the quantized light-matter interactions, a linearized dispersion approximation (LDA) was widely used in wQED under the conditions of weak coupling and narrow photonic bandwidth. However, a growing number of strong-coupling wQED experiments have called the validity of LDA into question. Here, by investigating giant atoms coupled to a semi-infinite waveguide, we propose a principle to judge the validity of LDA. We find that the decoherence of the atoms exhibits rich dynamical behaviors determined by different numbers of bound states in and out of the continuum (BICs and BOCs) formed in the energy spectrum of the total atom-photon system. Based on this, we show that despite the LDA can partially preserve some of BICs, it completely erases BOCs. This causes the dominant role of LDA in the atomic dynamics to break down. Providing a physical insight into the validity of LDA, our results lay a firm foundation for exploring fundamental physics and its application frontier in strong-coupling wQED platforms.
item.dc:creator: H. Z. Shen, Ze Wang, X. X. Yi, Jun-Hong An

item.title: Quantum Simulation of Electronic Structure using Quantum Density Functional Theory on a Programmable Integrated Photonic Circuit
item.description: arXiv:2611.04694v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum simulations of molecular electronic structure hold the potential for computational advantage but are inherently limited by the linear scaling of qubit requirements with respect to system size. Quantum Density Functional Theory (Q-DFT) addresses this constraint by reformulating the interacting many-body problem in terms of a non-interacting Kohn--Sham reference system. Here, we present and experimentally validate a Q-DFT algorithm that requires only $\mathcal{O}(\log_2(N))$ qubits to simulate a system of $N$ orbitals, thereby reducing resource overhead. More precisely, we solve the Kohn--Sham problem for the lithium hydride (LiH) molecule using the ensemble extension of the variational quantum eigensolver paradigm that minimizes the energy of the system in the subspace spanned by the ground and first excited states. To execute this task, we encode the problem with qubits on a quantum photonic platform, utilizing an architecture that combines a deterministic quantum dot single-photon source with a programmable integrated photonic circuit. By evaluating the molecular ground- and first excited-state properties, this work establishes a pathway for simulating larger molecular systems, demonstrating the viability of integrating qubit-efficient algorithms with advanced reconfigurable photonic hardware for near-term quantum chemistry applications.
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Adriano, Akilan Rajamani, Francesco Hoch, Farrokh Labib, Nadja Z. Zaouri, Eugenio Caruccio, Gonzalo Carvacho, Nicol\`o Spagnolo, Riccardo Albiero, Giacomo Corrielli, Francesco Ceccarelli, Jean-Sebastien Filhol, Roberto Osellame, Taira Giordani, Fabio Sciarrino, Nathan Shammah, Bruno Senjean

item.title: Temporal stretching of single-photon pulses by intra-cavity frequency conversion
item.description: arXiv:2611.04771v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spectral bandwidth and frequency mismatch between quantum light emitters and quantum components is a common problem in the realization of hybrid quantum information networks. Here we propose a simultaneous solution to both of these problems by using a free-space cavity with an embedded nonlinear crystal that, through frequency conversion, facilitates perfect coupling into a cavity mode. The slow leakage of the cavity effectively stretches the photon pulse, resulting in a much longer photon pulse at a different wavelength. We show that the amount of stretching is strictly limited by the finesse and length of the cavity. Including realistic internal losses in the cavity, we show that it is possible to stretch a photon by at least two orders of magnitude with high efficiency. The proposed setup can thus constitute a valuable addition to the toolbox of quantum information technologies.
item.dc:creator: Mathias L. H. Korsgaard, Eva M. Gonz\'alez-Ruiz, Anders S. S{\o}rensen

item.title: Bulk and edge states in Fibonacci-Bose-Hubbard clusters
item.description: arXiv:2611.04777v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the one- and two-boson energy subspaces of finite open Bose--Hubbard chains with Fibonacci-modulated hopping and zero on-site potential. Their spectra exhibit a hierarchy of bands and gaps, and a critical zero-energy mode for odd lengths, in agreement with prior research. For the singe-excitation subspace we find two families of length-invariant finite-energy states localized at the left cluster boundary. For the two-boson subspace, we report both doublon and separated-pair excitations in the form of Tamm/Shockley states localized near either end. In particular, the right-edge doublon states occur across all Fibonacci generations whereas the left-side states appear every second generation. We check numerically that the second-order perturbation theory accounts well for the structure of the spectrum and the edge states in the doublon subspace in the strong-coupling regime. The results are useful for future explorations of many-body physics beyond numerical tractability, specifically using near-term Josephson quantum simulators.
item.dc:creator: G. P. Fedorov, E. E. Konopleva, O. V. Astafiev

item.title: Mitigating small gaps in quantum annealing through recursive $XX-$catalyst construction
item.description: arXiv:2611.04840v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The introduction of $XX-$interactions, typically in the form of an additional catalyst Hamiltonian, has shown promise as a tool for gap enhancement in quantum annealing, allowing the algorithm to obtain optimal solutions with shorter run-times. However, the optimal placements of these couplings within the problem graph has been found to be highly setting-dependent. In this work, we propose an iterative catalyst-construction protocol for the removal of a common quantum annealing bottleneck known as perturbative crossings. The method utilises the measurements returned by successive annealing runs to effectively steer the algorithm away from the local optima in which it becomes trapped. First, we motivate a framework for $XX-$term selection based on perturbation theory and establish its effectiveness at removing perturbative crossings on scalable toy instances with up to $39$ spins, demonstrating a consistent performance both with increasing system size and number of local optima. We then simulate the recursive catalyst-construction method on a test set of $18-$spin maximum-weight independent set problems that are generated to produce annealing spectra with multiple perturbative crossings. We find that the protocol significantly outperforms both catalyst-free annealing and annealing with catalysts containing randomly selected $XX-$terms.
item.dc:creator: Natasha Feinstein, Sebastian Schulz, Robert J. Banks, Roopayan Ghosh, Kristel Michielsen, Sougato Bose, P A Warburton

item.title: Autonomous cooling of Kerr-cat qubits to minutes-long bit-flip times
item.description: arXiv:2611.04868v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum error correction becomes more hardware efficient when physical noise is strongly biased towards one error channel. Cat qubits realize such a bias by encoding information in two opposite coherent states of a superconducting oscillator, so that bit flips are exponentially suppressed with photon number while phase-flip rates increase only linearly. In Kerr-cat qubits, a driven double-well potential confines these states and enables fast coherent control, but excitations can induce interwell switching, limiting bit-flip times to milliseconds. Here we show that the nonlinear interaction generating the confinement can also cool these excitations. When an intra-well transition becomes resonant with a lossy readout mode, excitations are transferred out of the qubit and dissipated, as established by spectroscopy and relaxation measurements. We observe the predicted exponential scaling of Kerr-cat bit-flip times with photon number, reaching 450 s, over five orders of magnitude beyond previous demonstrations. Phase-flip rates remain consistent with intrinsic photon loss at operating points with seconds-long bit-flip times. We further demonstrate fast Z gates without measurable degradation of bit-flip protection and single-shot readout with a bit-flip probability below $10^{-6}$ per measurement. Autonomous cooling thus brings minutes-long bit-flip protection to Kerr-cat qubits while retaining fast coherent control, without additional cooling drives or circuit elements.
item.dc:creator: Sergey Hazanov, Mikhail Svintsov, Uri Goldblatt, Barkay Guttel, Fabien Lafont, Serge Rosenblum

item.title: Conditional Quantum Priors for Chaotic Fluid Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.04872v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neural networks that predict chaotic dynamics can reproduce short trajectories while misrepresenting statistics over long times. Quantum priors represent selected dynamical statistics through quantum generative models and provide statistical constraints for classical neural networks. Training a separate prior for each value of a system parameter, such as the Reynolds number, does not explicitly model how these statistics vary with that parameter. We learn a conditional quantum prior that approximates selected statistics of an invariant measure at unseen parameter values within the training range, without retraining. For Lorenz-63, the prior reduces mean Jensen-Shannon divergence by 56.9% relative to a classical multilayer perceptron with a comparable number of weights across 96 unseen parameter values. Across 101 values of the same parameter, the shared prior uses 84.7% fewer trainable weights than would be required by a separate quantum neural network at each value. We then use the learned prior to regularize classical neural networks, encouraging their autoregressive rollouts to better reproduce long-term statistics. For Kolmogorov flow at Reynolds number $Re=1000$, prior regularization reduces forecast mean squared error by 66.0% over 318 steps relative to the classical baseline without prior regularization. We also implement a photonic quantum prior for noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices, achieving a mean Jensen-Shannon divergence of $4.58\times10^{-3}$ for Lorenz-63 and $2.59\times10^{-3}$ for Kolmogorov flow at unseen parameter values.
item.dc:creator: Shao-Bo Zhou, Yu-Ze Zhu, Hang Song, Xiang Zhao, Lin Yang, Xian-Min Jin

item.title: Quantum sensing of a weak drive signal in cascaded quantum van der Pol oscillators
item.description: arXiv:2611.04895v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We have constructed a quantum sensing system composed of two quantum van der Pol (vdP) oscillators. Coherent and dissipative couplings are combined to establish a generic nonreciprocal coupling between the two vdP subsystems. A weak driving signal to be measured is applied to an oscillator (probe system) and then transferred via non-reciprocal coupling to another oscillator (measurement system) that is easier to measure. This allows for the acquisition of information about the driving strength of the signal being measured. For the classic cascaded dual vdP oscillators, complete non-reciprocal coupling yields a much higher susceptibility than a single classical vdP oscillator alone. For the quantum vdP system, the sensitivity generally does not diverge at the zero driving force point. When only dissipative coupling and two-particle loss are present, the system will have a dark mode at the zero driving force point, which enables the measurement precision to ultimately reach the Heisenberg limit in the time domain. Enhancing incoherent driving can effectively resist dissipation and thereby improve measurement precision. Moreover, in the strong incoherent driving regime, the improvement factor of non-reciprocal coupling over reciprocal coupling in terms of measurement precision tends to infinity as the two-particle loss rate of the measurement system approaches zero.
item.dc:creator: Dong Xie, Chungling Xu

item.title: Fast verification of fault tolerant magic state preparation circuits with the CNOT + T gate set
item.description: arXiv:2611.04909v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Magic state preparation is often among the most expensive operations in a fault tolerant quantum computation. One obstacle to coming up with better magic state preparation circuits lies in verifying their fault tolerance properties, as it is difficult to verify either by hand or in software that a very large number of combinations of faults do not give rise to high-weight or logical errors, especially in a non-Clifford circuit. In this work, we propose the use of the CNOT + T gate set to fault-tolerantly prepare a large class of magic states. We consider the propagation of Pauli faults within CNOT + T circuits and derive properties similar to those of Pauli faults within Clifford circuits, with a view to verifying fault tolerance as efficiently as possible. We present Comb, a library that can verify the fault tolerance of CNOT + T magic state preparation circuits, and demonstrate its use in verifying the fault tolerance of distance three and distance five magic state preparation circuits in minutes on a laptop. We present a distance five magic state preparation circuit that was discovered using Comb. As an independent confirmation of Comb's correctness we compare its findings to circuit-level noisy simulations for several magic state preparation circuits.
item.dc:creator: Selwyn Simsek, Callum Macpherson, Chris N. Self, David Amaro

item.title: Transferable Lindblad Variational Ansatz for Accelerated Steady-State Preparation
item.description: arXiv:2611.04919v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Open quantum systems naturally relax toward steady states that underpin diverse nonequilibrium phenomena and quantum technologies. We independently control the coherent and dissipative constituents of a Lindblad generator to construct a variational product formula, termed the Lindblad variational ansatz (LVA), that accelerates steady-state preparation over natural relaxation through an optimized preparation path. The protocol consists of small-system learning, continuation to greater depth, and transfer to larger systems, followed when needed by reference-free post-training on quantum simulators. We demonstrate LVA in a bulk-dissipative Ising chain and a boundary-driven Heisenberg chain, where transferred protocols achieve matched preparation accuracies with fewer generator blocks than time-optimized first- and second-order Trotter formulas. The acceleration arises from coordinated endpoint preparation: earlier controls shape the dissipative-mode amplitudes so that the final dissipative step brings multiple components simultaneously close to their target values. Our results suggest a route to open-system quantum simulation that combines classical training on small systems with deployment and optional refinement on larger quantum devices.
item.dc:creator: Yun-Zhuo Fan, Dan-Bo Zhang

item.title: Substantially Improved Rate and Distance for Addressable Transversal Phase Gates
item.description: arXiv:2611.04964v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An important ingredient in fault-tolerant quantum computation is asymptotically good codes with fully addressable transversal non-Clifford gates. Existing constructions, however, provide only small explicit guarantees for rate and relative distance. Here, we substantially improve these guarantees for fully addressable transversal phase gates at every fixed level $h\ge3$ of the Clifford hierarchy, using a cyclic encoding beyond the binary CSS framework. The encoding separates logical phase control from the joint design of rate and distance, enabling two constructions with different computational costs. A deterministic polynomial-time algebraic-geometric construction gives a common asymptotic lower bound of $52/(675h)$ on both quantities. A counting argument gives an exponential-time construction with exact verification, improving this bound by a factor of approximately $2.86$. We further establish a universal upper bound for codes supporting fully addressable transversal single-qubit phase gates. Within our cyclic encoding framework, we obtain a stronger upper bound that is approximately $1.28$ times the lower bound achieved by our exponential-time construction. As concrete examples, we construct codes with $48$ and $90$ physical qubits supporting fully addressable transversal $T$ gates. These results narrow the gap between achievable code parameters and addressability bounds, providing quantitative targets for further improvements in efficient code constructions.
item.dc:creator: Bujiao Wu, Tongyin Lin, Bin Cheng

item.title: Synchronization Mpemba Effect
item.description: arXiv:2611.04994v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the synchronization Mpemba effect, in which a less synchronized initial state overtakes a more synchronized one, and demonstrate it in dissipatively coupled quantum van der Pol oscillators. Within a graph-Laplacian framework, we show that for two oscillators, the mechanism is a competition between a slowly decaying collective background and a fast transverse transient, equivalently an exchange between relative-mode displacement and phase-fluctuation errors. The same decomposition extends to networks: the synchronization error splits into transverse Laplacian modes, yielding closed-form crossing times from eigenvalue separations and initial mode weights, and a sufficient screening criterion. With only these eigenvalues entering, the rule is topology independent: crossing times of different networks collapse onto a single spectral-gap line. Thus, quantum many-body dynamics can be designed and controlled at low dimension without constructing the exponentially large Liouvillian, opening a route to quantum synchronization as a resource.
item.dc:creator: Yan Li, Wenlin Li, Xingli Li

item.title: Ergotropy Activation and Coherence in Dissipatively Charged Quantum Batteries
item.description: arXiv:2611.05010v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum batteries can exploit quantum resources to enhance energy storage and work extraction, and recent experimental progress has brought their implementation closer to reality. In realistic settings, however, environmental dissipation is unavoidable, making dissipative charging a physically relevant operating regime. Here we investigate ergotropy in dissipatively charged quantum batteries, focusing on interaction-induced work extraction. For two coupled two-level systems (TLSs), we derive exact analytical expressions for the total, coherent, and incoherent ergotropy in both resonant and detuned configurations. We show that, in the resonant case, ergotropy is activated only above a critical coupling associated with an interaction-induced energy-level crossing, whereas detuning enables ergotropy already in the weak-coupling regime. Moreover, quantum coherence, although necessary for coherent work extraction, is not by itself sufficient to guarantee nonzero coherent ergotropy. In the strong-coupling regime, the resonant setup reaches the maximum ergotropy at a finite coupling strength, whereas the detuned setup approaches the same limit only asymptotically. Extending the analysis to a periodic XX spin chain of $N$ TLSs, we analytically derive the finite-temperature coupling threshold for ergotropy activation and show that it scales as $1/N$ in the large-$N$ limit. These results identify frequency detuning, interaction strength, and system size as key control parameters for ergotropy generation in open quantum batteries.
item.dc:creator: Hui-Yu Yang, Kang-Yuan Chen, Kun Zhang, Yang-Yang Chen, Xiao-Hui Wang

item.title: On Revolutionizing Power Systems: Suitability of Quantum Computing-Ready Pipelines for Stochastic Unit Commitment Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2611.05030v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern unit commitment (UC) scenarios, particularly those involving uncertainties from demand fluctuations and renewable energy sources, pose significant challenges to traditional optimization methods due to the large search spaces they encompass. This paper proposes a quantum computing-ready optimization pipeline for deterministic and stochastic UC, integrating classical, quantum-inspired, quantum annealing, and hybrid quantum-classical solvers across test systems, including the IEEE 118-bus system. A novel Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) reformulation accommodates generator scaling and 24-hour scheduling horizons with compact Boolean logic penalties for startup, cooldown, and spinning reserve constraints. A divide-and-conquer strategy and Quantum Computing Monte Carlo (QCMC) simulation address scalability across 27,730 uncertainty scenarios, reducing compilation time by up to two orders of magnitude. Experimental results demonstrate the pipeline's ability to achieve efficient, scalable, and accurate UC optimization under uncertainty: the hybrid quantum method approach matches the classical baseline, reduces stochastic UC runtime from 40.76 to 14.79 hours, and characterizes pure quantum annealing as limited to small systems with 0.22% to 2.18% encoding errors and constraint violations.
