Under explicit operational assumptions, we prove that the affine hull of the achievable behaviours is described exactly by the equalities stating that each joint output statistic depends only on the inputs that can reach the agents involved, so that a violated equality identifies both the statistic and the missing input. One binary message per event already attains this affine hull, so message capacity restricts which behaviours are achievable without being visible to any equality. We apply the result to one-bit broadcast and relay hierarchies for two and three agents, and to low-order projections of the local polytope.
item.dc:creator: M. Haider Akbar, Onur Pusuluk, \"Ozg\"ur E. M\"ustecapl{\i}o\u{g}lu

item.title: All-optical room-temperature spin coherence of aqueous asymmetrically chelated Cu(II) for chemoselective discrimination
item.description: arXiv:2610.24925v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Harnessing molecular electron spins as responsive quantum sensors in ambient water requires bridging ultrafast all-optical readout with selective chemical recognition. Here, we overcome the intrinsic magneto-optical sluggishness of 3d transition-metal complexes--which previously restricted all-optical detection to high concentrations of ~1 M--through a coordination-driven symmetry-breaking strategy. Coordinating aqueous Cu(II) with EDTA imposes a non-centrosymmetric ligand field with enhanced metal-ligand covalency, relaxing Laporte restrictions and amplifying d-d transition dipole moments. This design enables room-temperature all-optical initialization and readout of electron spin coherence down to 100 {\mu}M with an apparent dephasing time T_2^*~0.54 ns. Crucially, the chelated complex chemoselectively discriminates amino acid biomolecules: histidine binding induces a pronounced, concentration-dependent prolongation of T_2^* to ~0.8 ns, whereas glycine produces no measurable effect. These results transform spin dephasing into a chemically informative observable, opening avenues toward microwave-free, analyte-responsive quantum sensing in complex aqueous environments.
item.dc:creator: Jinlei Li, Qiaoyun Wu, Qiaoqiao Shao, Zhubin Hu, Haitao Sun, Zhenrong Sun, Donghai Feng

item.title: Marginal bunching for \textit{in situ} certification of multiparticle indistinguishability
item.description: arXiv:2610.25471v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose an \textit{in situ} method for certifying the multiparticle indistinguishability of identical bosons or fermions in generic linear interferometers. For particles occupying distinct input ports, the method uses two-particle marginal bunching or anti-bunching probabilities to bound full multiparticle indistinguishability through Aldous' spectral gap theorem. For Haar-random unitary interferometers, the number of experimental runs required to estimate this bound to a prescribed precision, at fixed confidence, is polynomial in the particle number, the interferometer size, and the inverse precision, with high probability over the choice of interferometer. Losses are incorporated without conditioning on particle survival. The method is particularly suited to certifying photon indistinguishability in large-scale interference experiments, including Boson Sampling experiments targeting quantum computational advantage.
item.dc:creator: Valery Shchesnovich

item.title: Seeing Why: Exact Evidence Maps for Quantum and Optical Image Classifiers
item.description: arXiv:2611.01993v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: When an image classifier decides, we can usually only estimate why. For quantum and all-optical classifiers that act linearly on amplitude-encoded pictures up to the measurement, with no trained classical network before or after them, each class's Born probability above its no-information share, $P_g - b_g$, splits exactly into contributions of the encoded amplitudes, shown as Born evidence maps (BEM) over the picture. The split itself follows from known results on quadratic forms: with the transmitted light held fixed, it is what Integrated Gradients from a zero baseline and the Shapley value give. What we add is a way to measure it on the hardware that classifies, from class probabilities on a quantum chip or from camera frames on a lens bench, with no gradient circuit and no light sent backwards; a $g\times g$ map takes $1 + 2g^2$ runs. Deleting the 5% of pixels with the highest evidence drops accuracy from 73% to 9%, as occlusion does with 1,024 extra runs per picture, whereas gradient saliency removes much less. The classifiers share one architecture, a Fourier-plane mask followed by a brickwall circuit on qubits or by phase plates on a lens bench, read by a fixed Born headroom readout with no trained parameter; centring each picture on its own mean lets dark features count as much as bright ones. In simulation, four phase plates at a single wavelength reach 72.3% on Caltech-10 colour photographs. On IBM's ibm_kingston, with the mask applied before approximate loading, 300 test pictures were classified at 37.7% against 10% by chance (56.3% in exact simulation), and $2\times2$ maps of ten correctly classified pictures, one per class chosen by a stated rule, measured on the chip, agreed with the exact ones ($r = 0.77$). The maps also revealed a shortcut in the data; as the trim that removed it was chosen on test pictures, the Caltech-10 results are exploratory.
item.dc:creator: Teerawat Tongloy, Rangsan Jomtarak

item.title: Classical and Quantum Logics with Multiple Non-Equivalent and Non-Isomorphic Models
item.description: arXiv:2611.02070v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Both quantum and classical logics have several mutually non-equivalent and non-isomorphic models as has repeatedly been proved in the literature. Yet, several authors have recently come with criticisms of this result. In this paper, we show that the criticisms are either unfounded or wrong.
item.dc:creator: Mladen Pavicic

item.title: Spin SYK-dot chains: entanglement bound and resource estimates towards a quantum advantage
item.description: arXiv:2611.03207v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Ground states of Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK)-type models are volume-law entangled, which makes them costly both for tensor networks and for quantum hardware simulations. Thus, it remains unclear where quantum hardware could outperform classical simulation of such models. In this work, we study a spin SYK-dot chain, in which q dense SYK dots of p qubits are joined by single ZZ bonds of strength K. The entanglement across any cut is then bounded by floor(p/2) ln 2 plus the inter-dot entanglement, and the two-qubit depth of one Trotter step is set by p alone. A resource estimate shows that a quantum advantage for the ground state could appear only for dots of about 15 to 21 qubits or more. There, a single Trotter step already requires two-qubit error rates of order 10^{-6}, beyond the reach of noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) hardware. We test the assumptions of this estimate with an imaginary-time matrix product state (MPS) that applies each dot as one block. It agrees with exact diagonalisation at (p, q) = (6, 2). At (5, 2), a variational circuit with the same dot-plus-link layout comes within 3.6% of the exact energy, and noisy simulations show that its fidelity decays as assumed in the resource estimate. At (8, 5), i.e., N = 40 qubits, the energy converges at bond dimension chi = 768, far below the exact value 2^20, and the inter-dot entanglement stays small and is set mainly by K. Out-of-time-order correlators across the links decay on a time scale that shrinks rapidly with |K|. Thus, the dot size p and the inter-dot coupling K together set the entanglement of the chain, and with it where a quantum advantage could appear.
item.dc:creator: Sayantan Dey, Abel Carreras, Siddhartha Patra

item.title: Exceptional Points and Optimized Encoding in Qubit Stabilizer Codes
item.description: arXiv:2611.03469v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Continuous blind stabilizer measurements turn stabilizer codes into a Liouvillian spectral problem in which Hamiltonian terms compete with dissipative error channels. We show that this competition generically enables Liouvillian exceptional points, whose occurrence at weak error rates is constrained by the code distance. Exceptional points are detrimental in this regime of error correction as they maximize the decay rate of encoded coherences. We then optimize the encoding of the logical qubit using the eigenmodes of the Lindblad operator. This phase-optimized encoding cancels the linear short-time decay of logical qubit coherences. We apply this encoding to the [[5,1,3]] code and demonstrate that it outperforms naive encoding methods near the exceptional point, improves the fidelity of a logical $\pi$ rotation and remains effective in the presence of additional weak error channels.
item.dc:creator: Yves Rottstaedt, Andrei I. Pavlov, Alexander Shnirman, Yuval Gefen, Bernd Rosenow

item.title: Multi-Partitioned Computing Quantum-Particle Approach: A Hybrid Quantum Framework for Fluid Flow
item.description: arXiv:2509.11276v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This study established a quantum-classical hybrid framework that integrates quantum computing paradigm with meshfree finite particle method. By harnessing quantum superposition and entanglement, it hybridized the critical computational kernels (termed as quantum finite particle method). A resource-efficient quantum computational strategy on multi-partitioned zones was proposed, which leverages a fixed small-scale quantum circuit as a fundamental processing unit to handle inner product for arbitrarily sized arrays. This approach employs iterative nesting of the quantum-core operation to accommodate varying input dimensions while maintaining hardware feasibility throughout. Motivated with developed quantum framework, the novel numerical discretization for hybrid quantum computational particle dynamics can be derived commonly and applied in fluid flows. Through a sequence of numerical experiments purposefully, the proposed numerical model was thoroughly validated and analyzed. Results demonstrate that integrating quantum computing to hybridize conventional linear combinations of particle dynamics serves as a novel computing paradigm. By further extending into the numerical investigation of viscoelastic, highly elastic, and purely elastic fluids under high Weissenberg number conditions, the applicability of simulation framework is broadened. Despite bottlenecks in quantum hardware and computational efficiency on this process, these advances offer critical insights for transitioning quantum-enhanced fluid simulation to practical engineering applications.
item.dc:creator: Yudong Li, Wenkui Shi, Zhihao Qian, Yan Li, Chunfa Wang, Ling Tao, Zhuojia Fu, Moubin Liu, Zhiqiang Feng

item.title: Roadmap to Quantum Aesthetics
item.description: arXiv:2602.08363v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Quantum mechanics occupies a central position in contemporary science while remaining largely inaccessible to direct sensory experience. This paper proposes a roadmap to quantum aesthetics that examines how quantum concepts become aesthetic phenomena through artistic mediation rather than direct representation. Two complementary and orthogonal approaches are articulated. The first, a pioneering top-down approach, employs text-prompt-based generative AI to probe quantum aesthetics as a collective cultural construct embedded in large-scale training data. By systematically modulating the linguistic weight of the term "quantum," generative models are used as experimental environments to reveal how quantum imaginaries circulate within contemporary visual culture. The second, a bottom-up approach, derives aesthetic form directly from quantum-mechanical structures through the visualization of quantum-generated data, exemplified here by hydrogen atomic orbitals calculated from the Schr\"odinger equation. These approaches are framed not as competing methods but as intersecting paths within a navigable field of artistic research. They position quantum aesthetics as an emergent field of artistic research shaped by cultural imagination, computational mediation, and physical law, opening new directions for artistic practice and pedagogy at the intersection of art, data, artificial intelligence and quantum science.
item.dc:creator: Ivan C. H. Liu, Hsiao-Yuan Chen

item.title: Thermalization with Gaussian Quantum Cellular Automata
item.description: arXiv:2606.05542v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the long-time dynamics of many-body bosonic lattice systems under translation-invariant Gaussian quantum cellular automata. We formulate two sets of conditions on GQCAs which separately guarantee thermalization of any state on the local Weyl algebra to the infinite temperature state, whenever the state is locally normal and has uniformly bounded particle density. Our main intermediate result is a quantum many-body generalization of the classic Riemann-Lebesgue lemma which is a bound on expectation values of local Weyl operators involving their support and the state's particle density.
item.dc:creator: Roman Geiko, Jake Gerenraich

item.title: Measurement-induced spatially nonuniform fluctuations of the local particle number and their crossover in a quasiperiodic free-fermion chain
item.description: arXiv:2607.03799v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study continuously monitored dynamics of a quasiperiodic free-fermion chain defined on a Fibonacci lattice. We focus on fluctuations of the local particle number, which do not exhibit quasiperiodic spatial modulation in the unitary limit. Remarkably, we demonstrate that they exhibit a nonuniform spatial pattern originating from the quasiperiodic long-range order under continuous measurement. Furthermore, employing both physicaland perpendicular-space analyses, we elucidate that a measurement-induced crossover emerges in fluctuations due to the interplay between the incommensurate modulation and the continuous measurement. While weak measurement yields a distribution reflecting the long-range spatial structure of the quasiperiodic system, an increase in measurement strength alters the distribution into one dominated by the local environment of each site. A structure-factor analysis further reveals that the weak-measurement regime is characterized by two dominant Bragg peaks corresponding to the golden-mean modulation, whereas the strong-measurement regime exhibits the characteristic Bragg-peak hierarchy of the Fibonacci pattern. We also elucidate that the measurement-induced crossover emerges in other physical quantities such as connected correlation functions. These findings offer insights into nonequilibrium quasiperiodic phenomena emerging in continuously monitored dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Toranosuke Matsubara, Kazuki Yamamoto

item.title: Entanglement Asymmetry in Random Quantum Automata
item.description: arXiv:2607.07556v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the subsystem entanglement asymmetry in random quantum automaton ensembles, which are generated by permuting the basis states in the Hilbert space and applying global phase shifts. We compute the ensemble average of the $U(1)$ subsystem asymmetry in different connectivity geometries, showing that the late-time limit of the ensemble associated to a 2-local circuit geometry coincides with the all-to-all ensemble average. By focusing on different subsystem sizes, we demonstrate that, similarly to Haar-random circuits, the system locally symmetrizes. However, in sharp contrast to the Haar-random setting, the scale at which symmetrization happens depends on the initial state, a phenomenon we associate with the interplay of conservation of the participation entropy and the uniform exploration of charge sectors. Additionally, we connect the growth of the subsystem asymmetry to the subsystem coherence and show that their growth is characterized by the same symmetrization scale.
item.dc:creator: Olalla A. Castro-Alvaredo, D\'avid Sz\'asz-Schagrin, Michele Mazzoni

item.title: Circuit and Krylov complexity of primordial perturbations of modified gravity in inflation
item.description: arXiv:2607.09408v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Taking canonical scalar field inflation as the reference case, we investigate the circuit and Krylov complexities of primordial curvature perturbations in an \(f(\phi,R)\) modified gravity inflation. We derive the evolution equations for the squeezed strength \(r_k\) and squeezed angle \(\varphi_k\), and calculate the circuit complexity, Krylov complexity, Krylov entropy, Lanczos coefficients, and effective dissipative contribution. Compared with the canonical model, the squeezed strength \(r_k\) grows more slowly in the modified gravity inflation and continues to exhibit oscillations after horizon exit. Consequently, the spreading in Krylov space is suppressed and modulated through the relation \(K=\sinh^2 r_k\). Modified gravity also changes the squeezed angle, thereby modifying the phase-space correlations and enhancing the oscillatory behavior of the circuit complexity. In the presence of modified gravity effects, information loss is suppressed before horizon exit, whereas it barely affects information loss after horizon exit. For the parameters considered, the Lyapunov exponent and Lanczos coefficients indicate that modified gravity has little effect on the effective degree of quantum chaoticity. These results show that \(f(\phi,R)\) modified gravity primarily reorganizes the amplitude, phase, complexity, and information loss dynamics of primordial quantum fluctuations.
item.dc:creator: Tao Li, Hai-Bing Fu

item.title: Eddy currents and current reversal in curved magnetic thin-film Josephson junctions
item.description: arXiv:2607.16399v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Real-space geometric curvature in magnetic thin films introduces a controllable mechanism for tailoring the pathways of superconducting steady-state Josephson currents via the proximity effect. We present a generalized Green's function method for calculating diffusive transport in arbitrarily curved surfaces, and show how the competing mechanisms of curvature and distance regulate conversion between different superconducting pairings in a proximity-coupled ferromagnet. We show how this dictates the distribution of current density, with the possibility of curvature-controlled current density manipulation, induced eddy currents and current reversal.
item.dc:creator: Einar Skoglund, Maxim A. Tj{\o}tta, Sol H. Jacobsen

item.title: Freezing Swampland: A Krylov Complexity Diagnostic for the Weak Gravity Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2607.23747v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose a quantum-information-theoretic perspective on the Weak Gravity Conjecture through the behavior of Krylov spread complexity. For a charged thermofield double state holographically dual to an AdS Reissner--Nordstr\"om black hole, we show that the extremal limit on the black-hole side is accompanied by an effective freezing of Krylov spreading. In this regime, the return amplitude becomes effectively a pure phase, and the corresponding Krylov spread is suppressed. We then incorporate charged matter and study the effect of Schwinger pair production in the near-horizon region. Within this semiclassical near-extremal analysis, the frozen behavior is lifted once an allowed discharge channel is opened, and the dynamics become nontrivial again. This suggests a possible complexity-based diagnostic of a characteristic physical consequence of the Weak Gravity Conjecture: the availability of a superextremal charged state that can mediate discharge. More broadly, our results point to a connection between the swampland program, black-hole physics, and quantum information theory.

item.title: Observation of s-p Coupling in Ultralong-Range Rydberg Molecules
item.description: arXiv:2608.09950v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Ultralong-range Rydberg molecules, formed by the interaction between a highly excited Rydberg atom and a ground-state atom, provide a unique platform for exploring quantum phenomena spanning nanometer- to micrometer distances as well as exotic few-body interactions. The molecular binding arises from electron-atom scattering, which is conventionally described by an independent s- and p-wave channels picture. Here we report the experimental observation of s-p coupling in Rb(nS)-Rb(5S) ultralong-range Rydberg molecules via high-resolution photoassociation spectroscopy. By varying the principal quantum number n from 31 to 36, we resolve an avoided crossing between the s- and p-wave molecular states: whenever a vibrational level bound by the p-wave well approaches one bound by the s-wave well in energy, the two states are mixed by the off-diagonal coupling U_sp, and the shifted s-wave level is identified, which is consistent with theoretical predictions. This mixing is most pronounced for low-node p-wave molecules, whose binding energies lie closer to those of the s-wave molecules. The resulting level repulsion and redistribution of spectral intensity reveal the mixed s-p character of ultralong-range Rydberg molecules and provide a more precise molecular spectroscopy.

item.title: Random Garbage Creates Exponential Quantum Query Separations
item.description: arXiv:2609.03628v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove an exponential separation between standard (XOR) quantum queries and forward-erasing queries for a Boolean property of injective functions, answering a question of Aaronson~\cite{Aaronson2021Open}. We also obtain an exponential separation for a Boolean promise problem on permutations, where forward in-place queries are unitary but inverse queries are not supplied. Our construction follows Aaronson's suggestion of appending fixed random garbage to a Simon function. Let $X=\{0,1\}^n$ and $N=2^n$. We use the injection $f_{h,r}(x)=(h(x),x,r_x)$, where $h:X\to X$ is promised to be either a permutation or a Simon function, and $r:X\to X$ is an arbitrary tag table that is reused on every query. The resulting problem is solvable with at most $n+2$ standard queries, but requires $\Theta(\sqrt N)$ forward-erasing queries, matching classical collision sampling. Embedding these instances into permutations, with the copy of $x$ replaced by a single bit that keeps the embedding injective, gives a promise problem on permutations of $L=4N^2$ elements that requires $O(\log L)$ standard queries versus $\Theta(L^{1/4})$ forward in-place queries. The lower bounds use the recording method. We replace each query by a nearby contraction that records cells of a purified tag table. After $T$ queries, tracing out the purified tag table yields a sum of positive-semidefinite contributions, each depending on $h$ at no more than $T$ addresses. A query-by-query hybrid bounds the trace-norm difference between the actual and auxiliary final operators by $O(T/\sqrt N)$. Random permutations and random Simon functions have the same restriction distribution on such a set unless it contains a hidden Simon pair, an event of probability $O(T^2/N)$. Consequently, the actual final states in the two cases remain close unless $T=\Omega(\sqrt N)$, giving the required lower bounds.

item.title: Distinguishability Transitions from Global Quantum Snapshots
item.description: arXiv:2609.09296v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Quantum states generated by generic time evolution are locally featureless: local measurements return random outcomes that are identical for all states. However, global snapshots in the computational basis are surprisingly effective at distinguishing between quantum states. We explore the ability of Bayesian classifiers to discriminate between many random quantum states using a small number of measurement outcomes. We identify a phase transition in the ability of the classifier to distinguish between $k$ candidate states with $m$ shots controlled by the variable $x = m / \ln k$, and derive the threshold value $x_c$. We extend our results to low-depth circuits near the onset of anti-concentration, as well as to noisy circuits and phase-random states.

item.title: Noncommutative sharp Hausdorff-Young inequality
item.description: arXiv:2609.10424v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove the sharp Hausdorff--Young inequality on quantum euclidean spaces. Our result implies the sharp Hausdorff--Young constants for the Weyl transform. The key ingredients are a sharp Hessian comparison inequality and a novel flow related to the mixed- norm of noncommutative Gabor transform; the Hessian comparison leads to the monotonicity of the flow. We also apply the same flow technique to prove the sharp Hausdorff--Young inequalities on Heisenberg groups and the affine group.

item.title: Deterministic Hypergraph SYK: Melonic Dominance and Maximal Chaos Without Disorder Averaging
item.description: arXiv:2609.19255v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that the leading melonic structure of the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model can be realized by a single sparse Majorana Hamiltonian, without disorder averaging. In our deterministic hypergraph SYK model (hSYK), $N$ Majorana fermions interact through $O(dN)$ terms with uniform couplings, arranged on a fixed $q$-uniform, $d$-regular hypergraph. If the hypergraph is linear, has few short cycles, and is a spectral expander, then at large $d$ the two-point function obeys the melonic Schwinger-Dyson equation site by site. The leading thermodynamics are therefore those of SYK, and at leading order in $1/d$ every bilocal fluctuation other than the Schwarzian is gapped. The four-point ladder splits into scrambling modes labeled by eigenvalues of the site adjacency operator. At strong coupling, the uniform mode is maximally chaotic, and a non-uniform mode grows only if its eigenvalue exceeds $1/(q-1)$. Exact diagonalization of single instances with $N\le24$ agrees with the melonic two-point function and thermodynamics more closely than dense SYK of the same size, shows Wigner-Dyson level statistics, and reproduces the predicted mode structure of out-of-time-order correlators. Numerically, random linear hypergraphs typically satisfy these conditions, and for $d>q$ also avoid emergent symmetries. The model is a natural candidate for quantum simulation.

item.title: Gravitational anomaly spectroscopy of a Kitaev spin liquid
item.description: arXiv:2610.38704v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The chiral central charge $c$ measures the gravitational anomaly of a two-dimensional topological phase and fixes the heat current along its edge. It has been accessed through thermal transport, where phonons complicate the signal, or through wave-function probes that need a pure ground state. Here we show that a calibrated combination of directional edge absorption weights determines $c$. A modulation of the edge couplings that travels along the edge is absorbed according to the Virasoro algebra, and a static change of the same couplings measures the unknown probe normalization. Two harmonics then cancel the dependence on the edge state, so the estimator returns $c$ in any state of the ideal edge theory. A ratio of line weights with and without a vison gives the conformal spin of the Ising anyon. For the Kitaev honeycomb model, exact calculations recover $c=1/2$ and $h_\sigma=1/16$ to $10^{-5}$ and give $c$ within about $1\%$ on 96 spins. Compiled into gate circuits on the physical spins of a square-lattice quantum simulator, the protocol returns $c$ within $5\%$ on 48 qubits. For stochastic gate errors it requires two-qubit error rates of $10^{-6}$ to $10^{-5}$.
